cards.text: The apostle Paul has just seen a vision of a man of Macedonia pleading, 'Come over to Macedonia and help us.' So the team sails from Troas straight to Samothrace, and the next day on to Neapolis. And notice the writer starts saying 'we' here, friend, so he's on that boat too.

cards.question: From Neapolis, the team heads to the Roman colony of ___, the leading city of that district of Macedonia.

cards.text: They stay in Philippi several days. Then on the Sabbath, they head outside the city gate and down to the river, where they expect to find a place of prayer.

cards.question: Down by the river, Paul's team sits down and speaks to the men who have gathered there.

cards.text: One of the women listening is Lydia from Thyatira, a dealer in purple cloth and a worshiper of God. PURPLE cloth! I own one white apron, friend, and it stays white for about four minutes.

cards.question: As Paul speaks, Lydia's heart opens to respond to his message. Who opens her heart?

cards.text: Lydia and her household are baptized. Then she tells the team, 'If you consider me a believer in the Lord, come and stay at my house.'

cards.question: Paul's team turns down Lydia's offer and stays somewhere else in Philippi.

cards.text: Lydia talks them into it, and after an invitation like THAT, who's saying no? One day on the way to the place of prayer, they're met by a slave girl with a spirit of divination, and her masters make a large income off her fortune-telling.

cards.question: This slave girl follows Paul and the team. What does she keep shouting about them?

answers.text: They serve the Most High God
They are false prophets in disguise
They are thieves from the harbor

cards.text: She keeps this up for many days, until Paul gets so aggravated he turns around and speaks to the spirit. I love my oven timer, friend, but if it beeped for MANY DAYS, I'd turn around too.

cards.question: Paul commands the spirit to come out of her in the name of ___ ___.
When Paul gives the command, the spirit leaves the girl at that very moment.

cards.text: Now her owners see that their hope of making money is gone. Uh oh.

cards.question: What do the girl's owners do to Paul and his traveling partner Silas?

answers.text: Beg them to bring the spirit back
Pay them to leave the city

cards.text: They haul Paul and Silas into the marketplace and up to the magistrates. First thing the owners point out: these men are Jews.

cards.question: What do the owners accuse Paul and Silas of doing in Philippi?

answers.text: Stealing the girl from her masters

cards.text: Notice they never say one word about the money. Then the crowd joins in, and the magistrates have Paul and Silas stripped, beaten with rods and thrown into prison.

cards.question: The jailer is ordered to guard Paul and Silas securely, so he puts them in the inner cell and fastens their feet in the stocks.

cards.text: Inner cell, feet locked in the stocks. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, friend, and at least I could roll around a little.
Paul and Silas are locked in the inner cell, feet fastened in the stocks. It gets to be about midnight. Me? I'd be up too, and I'd be COMPLAINING.

cards.question: About midnight in that prison cell, what are Paul and Silas doing?

answers.text: Praying and singing hymns to God
Quietly planning a way to escape

cards.question: While Paul and Silas pray and sing, the other prisoners are listening to them.

cards.text: Suddenly a strong earthquake shakes the foundations of the prison. I've been in a drawer when somebody slammed it, friend, and this is NOT that.

cards.question: At once all the prison doors fly ___ and everyone's chains come ___.

cards.text: The jailer wakes up and sees the prison doors open. He presumes the prisoners have escaped, so he draws his sword and is about to kill himself.

cards.question: Paul calls out to the jailer in a loud voice. What does Paul tell him?

answers.text: Don't harm yourself because we're all here
Run now before the magistrates find out
Put your sword down and set us free

cards.text: Doors open, chains loose, and NOBODY leaves? Friend, if that drawer had ever popped open like that, I'd have been gone so fast I'd have left my mustache behind.

cards.question: The jailer calls for lights, rushes in and falls trembling before Paul and Silas. Then he brings them out. What does he ask them?

answers.text: What must I do to be saved
Who sent this earthquake on us
How did your chains come loose

cards.question: Paul and Silas reply, "Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be ___, you and your household."

cards.text: Then Paul and Silas speak the word of the Lord to him and to everyone in his house. And at that hour of the night, the jailer washes their wounds.

cards.question: The jailer and his household wait a while before they are baptized.

cards.text: He brings Paul and Silas into his home and sets a meal before them. From the stocks to the jailer's table in ONE night, friend, and it took me YEARS just to get out of a drawer!

cards.question: The jailer and his whole household are rejoicing. Why?

answers.text: They have come to believe in God
The jailer has earned a reward

cards.text: When daylight comes, the magistrates send officers with the order: 'Release those men.' The jailer tells Paul they can go on their way in peace.

cards.question: But Paul tells the officers they were beaten publicly without a trial and thrown into prison, even though he and Silas are Roman ___.
Now the magistrates want to send Paul and Silas away secretly. What does Paul say the magistrates should do instead?

answers.text: Come themselves and escort them out
Pay them back for the beating
Put the slave girl's owners on trial

cards.text: The magistrates are alarmed to hear Paul and Silas are Roman citizens. The same men who ordered the rods now come in person to appease them, lead them out and ask them to leave the city.

cards.question: Before leaving Philippi, Paul and Silas go to Lydia's house to see the brothers.

cards.text: They encourage the brothers there, and then they leave the city. That's where we'll leave them for now, friend, because Paul's road is far from done.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 10 quotes "Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be ___, you and your household.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The apron joke doesn't match the fact. Lydia deals in purple cloth. The comparison is about Papa Dorin's white apron getting dirty, which is a different action. Most bakers would have to work out why 'PURPLE cloth!' leads to an apron that stays white for four minutes.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Silas first appears here, as a wrong answer, with no word on who he is. He isn't introduced until stop 1 card 15 ('his traveling partner Silas').

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card cites Acts 16:17-18, but it only tells verse 18 ('She keeps this up for many days', Paul grows aggravated and turns to the spirit). The shouting in verse 17 was already told and asked on card 10. The citation should be Acts 16:18.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Throwing the city into turmoil', comes from Acts 16:20 only, but the card cites Acts 16:20-21. Verse 21 gives how they supposedly did it, which isn't part of the answer.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: This card is a recap. Card 19 already covered the inner cell and the stocks (Acts 16:24). This card repeats that detail and adds only a joke, so it doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The card opens by repeating the inner cell and the stocks (Acts 16:24) for the third time in a row, after stop 1 cards 19 and 20. That's why its citation reaches back to verse 24. Only 'about midnight' (verse 25) is new.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: One wrong answer, 'Put your sword down and set us free', partly means the same as the right answer, 'Don't harm yourself because we're all here'. Telling a man about to kill himself to put his sword down is close to 'Do not harm yourself.' A baker could argue it's half right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This card tells nothing new. It reacts to doors, chains and Paul's 'We are all here', which cards 4 through 7 already covered, and it cites Acts 16:26-28 for a joke alone. The joke also strains the backstory. The drawer opened often in his years there, and a stamper couldn't run out of it.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The question says as fact that 'the magistrates want to send Paul and Silas away secretly.' In the text, that is Paul's own question in Acts 16:37 ('And now do they want to send us away secretly?'). It should be told as what Paul says.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
